originalTitle: Ethiopian death row inmates desperate to escape execution in Saudi Arabia call the BBC
title: Friends Far From Home: A Story from Ethiopia
content:
Hello, Amazing Explorers of Africa!

Hello everyone! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, bringing you a special story from our wonderful continent, Africa. Today, we have a story that is a little bit sad, but it's very important to know. It’s about some of our friends from a beautiful country right here in Africa, called Ethiopia. These friends are very far away from home, and they need our help. We are going to learn about where they are, what trouble they are in, and how people are trying to help them.

Who are our friends?

Imagine a country in Africa with amazing history, tall mountains, and some of the best coffee in the world! That’s Ethiopia! It’s a place where people have lived for thousands and thousands of years. Ethiopia is known for its kind people and its very unique culture. Many people from Ethiopia are very hardworking and always try their best to help their families. Sometimes, people from Ethiopia travel to other countries. They go to find new jobs or to learn new things, hoping to send money home to help their moms, dads, brothers, and sisters. Our story is about some of these brave Ethiopian people who traveled very, very far from their homes. Did you know? Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in the world! It has never been colonized by other countries, which makes its people very proud.

Where are they now?

These friends are not in Africa anymore. They are in a country called Saudi Arabia. Now, where is Saudi Arabia? It's a country in Asia, which is another big part of the world, very far from Ethiopia. You would have to fly over a big, blue ocean to get there! Saudi Arabia is known for its big deserts and sometimes very tall, shiny buildings. It’s a very different place from the green lands and mountains of Ethiopia. Our friends went there hoping to find good jobs and a better life. They wanted to earn money to help their families back home in Ethiopia. They packed their bags, said goodbye, and made the long journey, full of hope for the future. Did you know? Saudi Arabia is home to the biggest sand desert in the world! Imagine sand dunes as tall as a building!

What is the big problem?

Sadly, our Ethiopian friends in Saudi Arabia are in a very, very big trouble. They are in a place where they are waiting for a very serious punishment. It is a very sad and scary situation for them. They miss their homes, their families, and the familiar sights and sounds of Ethiopia very much. It must be a very lonely feeling to be so far away and in such a difficult situation. We don't know all the reasons why each person is in trouble, but we know they are scared and need support. It is important for everyone to follow the rules when they visit a new country. But sometimes, people can get into trouble even when they try their best. This big problem means they cannot go home, and they are facing something very scary. Did you know? Sometimes, when people travel for work, they might not understand all the rules of a new country, which can lead to problems.

Meet Tigray

Many of these people who are in trouble are from a special part of Ethiopia called Tigray. Tigray is a region in the northern part of Ethiopia. It has its own unique history, traditions, and a very strong culture. The people from Tigray are very proud of their homeland and their heritage. It's a place with ancient churches carved into rocks and a rich past. For these friends, being far from Ethiopia is hard enough, but being away from Tigray, their specific home, makes their sadness even bigger. Imagine missing your village, your friends, and your special foods from home. That’s how they must feel. Did you know? Some of the oldest Christian churches in the world are found in Tigray, Ethiopia, carved right out of solid rock!

Why did they call the BBC?

Our friends felt very alone and scared in Saudi Arabia. They wanted someone to listen to their story. They wanted the world to know about their big problem and to ask for help. So, they bravely called a very famous news company called the BBC. The BBC is a giant news company that tells stories to people all over the world, from Africa to Asia to America! They called the BBC because they hoped that by telling their stories, important people would hear and try to help them. It was a very brave thing for them to do, to speak out when they were in such a scary situation. They want people to know they are in trouble and need support and kindness. Did you know? The BBC started telling stories a very long time ago, in 1922! That's more than 100 years ago!

Who is trying to help?

When people hear sad stories like this, many kind-hearted people want to help. Governments, special groups that protect people, and even everyday people like you and me are trying to help our Ethiopian friends. They are talking to the leaders in Saudi Arabia, asking them to be kind. They are asking for a chance for our friends to be safe and maybe even go back home to their families. There are special groups called 'human rights' groups. These groups are like superheroes who fight to make sure everyone in the world is treated fairly and with respect. They work very hard to help people who are in trouble, no matter where they are from. It’s a big effort, but many people believe that everyone deserves kindness and a second chance. Did you know? The idea of 'human rights' means that every single person, no matter where they live or what they look like, should be treated well and have basic needs met.

A Message of Hope from Africa

This story is a little sad, but it also shows us how brave people can be, even when they are scared. It shows that when we tell our stories, others can listen and try to help. Let's all send our good wishes and hope to our friends from Ethiopia. We hope that they can be safe very soon and maybe, one day, go back home to their families and the beautiful lands of Ethiopia. Remember, being kind, listening to others, and helping those in need is one of the most important things we can do as amazing citizens of Africa and the world. Even from far away, our thoughts and hopes can make a difference. We will keep watching this story and hoping for the very best for our friends from Ethiopia. Let’s always remember to be kind! Did you know? Showing kindness can make you and the person you are kind to feel happier! It's a win-win!
summary: Many people from Ethiopia, especially from a place called Tigray, are in serious trouble far away in Saudi Arabia, and they called a news company called the BBC to tell their stories and ask for help.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows us that people from our own continent, Africa, sometimes travel far to find work and can face big problems, reminding us to be kind, understand different countries, and always hope for people to be safe and treated fairly.

originalTitle: Spain's PM blames traffickers after 60,000 migrants reach Ceuta from Morocco
title: Many Friends Moved Across the Water: News from Near Africa!
content:
Hello, Super Reporters and Amazing Kids!

Welcome to your special African News Corner! I'm your friendly reporter, ready to share important stories from our amazing continent and nearby places. Today, we have a story that happened very close to our home, in a country called Morocco, and a city called Ceuta. It's a story about many people, kind hearts, and how countries work together. Let's dive in!

What Happened This Week Near Our Continent?

Imagine a very special city called Ceuta. It’s a part of a country called Spain, but it's actually located right on the top edge of Africa, next to another country we know, Morocco! Last week, something big happened there. Many, many people, including lots of families, crossed from Morocco into Ceuta. It was a very big number of people – more than 60,000! That's like a whole lot of people, maybe more than live in your town or city! They walked or swam across a small bit of water to get there. Did you know? Africa is the second-largest continent in the whole wide world! Morocco is one of the beautiful countries on its northern tip.

Why Did So Many People Want to Go?

Sometimes, people move from one place to another. They might be looking for a new home, a safe place, or a better chance to find a good job. It’s a very big decision for families to move. These people hoped to find new opportunities in Spain, which is a country across the sea from Morocco. They felt that their lives might be better if they could reach Spain. Everyone wants to live happily and safely, right?

Who Are "Traffickers" and Why Are They Not Good?

The leader of Spain, who is called the Prime Minister (like the head boss of the country!), was very sad and worried about what happened. He said that some bad people, called "traffickers," might have been involved. "Traffickers" are grown-ups who are not kind. They trick people and sometimes promise them things that aren't true. They might tell people it's safe to travel in dangerous ways or that they will have a wonderful life if they pay money. But often, these promises are lies, and they put people in danger. The Prime Minister was very upset that these bad people might have encouraged others to cross over in unsafe ways. Did you know? It's always important to only trust grown-ups you know and who care about you, like your family and teachers. They will always keep you safe!

Where is Ceuta, Our Special City?

Let’s think about our map! Morocco is a country in North Africa. Spain is a country in Europe, just across a small bit of sea called the Strait of Gibraltar. Ceuta is a really interesting place because it's a city that belongs to Spain, but it's actually on the African side, right next to Morocco! So, it's like a little piece of Spain right on our continent. People can walk or swim across a very short border from Morocco to Ceuta. Did you know? Borders are like invisible lines that separate one country from another! Sometimes there are fences or guards, and sometimes it's just a line on a map.

What Happened Next? Most People Went Home.

It was a very busy time, but guess what? Most of the people who crossed into Ceuta went back home to Morocco very quickly. By Friday evening, most of the 60,000 people had returned. This means that many grown-ups from both Spain and Morocco worked together to help guide people back safely. It’s always good when countries help each other, isn't it? Things became much calmer in Ceuta after that.

Other Countries Were Watching Too!

When big things happen, other countries sometimes watch and worry. A country called Italy, which is also in Europe, saw what was happening. Italy is part of a special club of countries that have an agreement called "Schengen." This agreement makes it very easy for people to travel between these countries without lots of checks. But because so many people crossed into Spain, Italy got a little worried. So, Italy made their rules for visiting a bit stricter for a short time, just to be extra careful. They want to make sure everyone is safe and that people travel in the right ways. Did you know? The world has nearly 200 countries, and many of them work together on different things, just like friends playing a game!

Why Is This Story Important for Us?

This story reminds us of a few important things. It reminds us that many people in the world are looking for a better and safer life. It reminds us that leaders, like the Prime Minister of Spain, try very hard to keep everyone safe and to stop bad people from doing harm. And it reminds us that countries often need to talk to each other and work together when big challenges happen. It’s all about being kind, being safe, and finding good solutions. Let's always remember to be kind to everyone, no matter where they come from.

A Message From Your African News Reporter!

Thank you for listening, my wonderful friends! Remember, the world is a big place with lots of stories. It’s good to learn about them. Always be curious, always be kind, and keep shining bright! See you next time for more exciting news!
summary: Many people crossed from Morocco into a Spanish city called Ceuta, but most quickly returned home, while leaders discussed how to help people and stop bad grown-ups from tricking them.
whyMatters: This story is important because it shows how people sometimes move to find a better life, how countries work together to help, and why it's important for everyone to stay safe from bad people.

originalTitle: Most Australian teens still online three months after under-16 ban
title: News from Far Away! Being Safe Online!
content:
Hello, my amazing friends all over Africa! It's your friendly news reporter here. I hope you are all happy and ready to learn something new today. We are going to talk about something very important. It's about being safe when you play games or watch videos on a phone or computer.

News from a Faraway Land: Australia!

Far, far away from us, there is a big country called Australia. It has kangaroos and koalas! In Australia, the grown-ups who make rules, called the government, made a special rule. This rule was for young people, called teenagers. If you were younger than 16 years old, you were not supposed to be online on certain social media apps.

Why Did They Make This Rule?

Think about your favourite park. Your parents tell you to stay safe, right? Maybe don't talk to strangers. Don't run into the street. It's the same with the internet! The grown-ups in Australia wanted to keep their young people safe. They worried about some things online. One worry was spending too much time online. Sometimes, if we play games or watch videos for too long, our eyes get tired. We might forget to play outside. We might forget to do our homework! Our brains also need a break. Too much screen time can make it hard to sleep. **Did you know?** Many smart people say that playing outside helps your body grow strong and makes your brain smart too! It's good to play with friends in the sunshine. Another worry was about strangers. Just like in a park, there can be people online you don't know. Some people are not kind. They might pretend to be your friend. But they might not be good people. The grown-ups wanted to stop young people from talking to strangers online. Also, sometimes there are things online that are not good for young eyes. Like movies or games that are too scary. Or words that are not polite. The government wanted to protect the children from seeing these things. They really wanted the kids to be safe and happy.

What Happened After the Rule?

So, the rule was made. No social media for kids under 16! But then, something interesting happened. Some smart people made a report. A report is like a special book that tells you what happened. This report said that many young people, even after the rule, were still going online. Yes, that's right! Even with the rule, lots of teenagers found ways to use their favourite apps. This happened even after three whole months! It was like trying to stop a little river from flowing. The water found a different path!

How Did They Get Around the Rule?

You might wonder, "How did they do it?" Well, some young people used their older brother or sister's phone. Or maybe they used their mum or dad's account. It's like borrowing a big person's shoes. They don't quite fit, but you can still walk in them! Some also just clicked "yes" when the app asked if they were old enough. Even if they were not 16, they just said they were. It's easy to click a button! It's like when you want a cookie, and you say "yes please!" very quickly. This showed that making rules for the internet can be tricky. It's like trying to catch a speedy rabbit! The rabbit always finds a way to hide.

What Did the Grown-Ups Say Next?

After the report came out, the grown-ups in the Australian government talked about it. They said, "Hmm, this rule is not working perfectly." But they also said, "It is still a good idea!" They said they still believe it's important to help kids be safe online. Even if the rule didn't stop everyone, it made people think. It made parents talk to their kids about safety. And that is a very good thing! It's like planting a seed. Even if the plant doesn't grow huge right away, it's still growing.

What Can We Learn in Africa?

Now, why is this important for us here in Africa? Even though this happened far away in Australia, the idea is the same everywhere. Being safe online is important for every child! In Africa, more and more people are using phones and computers. We use them for school, for learning new things, and sometimes for fun games. It's wonderful to connect with people and learn! But we must always remember to be careful. **Did you know?** Many children in Africa are learning amazing things using the internet! They can learn about animals, about space, and even how to draw! We can learn from Australia's story. It tells us that rules are important. But even more important is to understand *why* the rules are there. It's about keeping us healthy and happy.

My Top Tips for Staying Safe Online (for My Amazing African Friends!)

1. **Always Ask a Grown-Up:** Before you go online, always ask your mum, dad, aunty, uncle, or older brother or sister. They can help you choose good things to see. They can help you understand the rules. 2. **Don't Talk to Strangers:** If someone you don't know tries to talk to you online, tell a grown-up right away. Don't tell them your name or where you live. Keep your secrets safe! 3. **Don't Share Private Things:** Never tell anyone your secret password. Never show pictures of your home or your school to people you don't know. Your private life is like a special treasure – keep it hidden! 4. **Take Breaks:** Don't spend too much time on the screen. Go outside and play! Help your family. Read a book. Let your eyes and your brain rest. Your body will thank you! 5. **Choose Good Games and Videos:** Ask a grown-up to help you find games and videos that are fun and good for your age. There are so many amazing things to learn and enjoy!

Let's Stay Smart and Safe!

So, my dear friends, remember this story from Australia. Grown-ups everywhere want to keep you safe. The internet is a big, exciting place. It's like a huge market with lots of wonderful things, but you need to know which path to take. By talking to your parents and listening to their advice, you can enjoy all the good things the internet has to offer. You can learn new things, connect with friends, and explore the world, all while staying safe and happy. Keep learning, keep playing, and always be kind! See you next time for more news!
summary: In Australia, a rule was made to keep young people under 16 safe by stopping them from using social media, but many still found ways to go online, showing that learning to be safe is very important everywhere.
whyMatters: This story matters because it helps us remember to be careful when we use phones or computers. Grown-ups want to keep us safe online from strangers or bad things, and by listening to them, we can learn to have fun and learn many things safely.

title: Helping Hands in a Special City!
content:
Hello from Your African News Friend!

Hi everyone! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, bringing you important stories from our amazing continent, Africa, and sometimes from places very close to us! Today, we have a story about a special city and how people are helping each other. It's a story about kindness, big journeys, and making sure everyone is safe.

Where is Ceuta? It's a Special City!

Imagine a city that is right next to a big, big sea, and it’s also very close to the country of Morocco in Africa. But guess what? This city, called Ceuta (say it: See-YOO-tah), is actually part of Spain! Yes, Spain is a country in Europe, far away, but they have this little piece of land right here in Africa. It’s like having a little part of a different country right next door! *Did you know?* Ceuta is a very unique place because it’s on the continent of Africa but is part of a European country. It has a beautiful coast with lovely beaches!

Many People Came to Ceuta

A little while ago, something very big happened in Ceuta. Lots and lots of people, including mummies, daddies, and even some children, came to Ceuta. They came from nearby countries, hoping to find a new, safe place to live or to find work for their families. It was like a very, very busy day, with many, many people arriving all at once! They wanted to find a better life, a place where they could be safe and happy.

Why Did They Come?

These people had a dream. They dreamed of finding good schools for their children, or good jobs so they could buy food and clothes for their families. Sometimes, it’s not easy to find these things where they used to live. So, they decided to make a very brave journey to Ceuta, hoping it would be a step towards a happier future. Imagine going on a very long trip to find something wonderful! *Did you know?* People sometimes move to new places for many reasons, like finding a good school, a new job, or to be safe from danger. It's called migration!

How Did They Get There?

Many of these brave people tried to get to Ceuta by the big blue sea. They swam, or used small boats, to cross the water. The sea can be very beautiful, but it can also be very strong and tricky. It’s a very dangerous journey to swim across the sea, especially if you don't have special safety gear or a strong boat. Sadly, because the journey was so difficult and dangerous, some people got very, very tired or had accidents. It’s very sad when people get hurt or don’t make it to safety. That's why it’s so important that people help each other, especially near big water. *Did you know?* The ocean is so big that it covers more than half of our planet Earth! It's beautiful but also needs to be respected. Always be careful near big water!

Lots of Helping Hands!

When all these people arrived, many grown-ups in Ceuta and Spain jumped into action to help. Police officers, rescue workers, doctors, and nurses worked very hard. They were like superheroes! They helped people who were tired or sick from their long journey. They gave them warm blankets, yummy food, and fresh water. They also looked after the children, making sure they were safe and had everything they needed. It’s amazing to see how many people want to help others when they are in need. They showed great kindness and care to everyone who arrived. They showed that even when things are difficult, people can come together to make a difference. *Did you know?* Helping others is one of the kindest things you can do! When you help someone, it makes both you and the other person feel good.

Going Back or Finding a Safe Spot

Now, after all the helping and caring, many of the people who came to Ceuta are slowly leaving. Some are going back to their homes, and others are going to other safe places where grown-ups can help them figure out their next steps. The grown-ups in charge, like the people who work for Spain, are making sure that everyone is looked after properly and safely. They are trying to make sure everything is organized and that everyone has a clear path forward. They want to make sure everyone is safe, and that the rules of the city are followed. It’s like when your teacher makes sure everyone has a turn or knows what to do next in class – it keeps things fair and safe for everyone.

What Can We Learn?

This story from Ceuta teaches us a few important things. First, it shows us how brave people can be when they are looking for a better life. Second, it shows us how important it is to be kind and help others, especially when they are in trouble. And third, it reminds us that safety is super important, especially when you are near the big sea. *Did you know?* Africa is the second-largest continent in the world! It has 54 different countries, all with unique cultures and amazing people.

A Message from Your Reporter!

So, my young friends, remember to always be kind to everyone you meet. Sometimes people come from far away, sometimes they are just next door. Everyone deserves kindness and help when they need it. And always remember to be safe, especially near water! Keep shining bright, and I’ll be back soon with more news from our wonderful world!
summary: Many people came to the special city of Ceuta looking for a new home, and grown-ups are helping them be safe and find new places to go.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows how important it is for people to help each other, especially when someone needs a safe place or a fresh start. It reminds us to be kind and safe.
